title: runtime-vignettes-and-mitigation-ideas-may-2026
content:
Executive summary:

This note is a compact synthesis of recurring customer vignettes related to inference runtime friction (latency variability, cold-starts, and KV cache behavior) gathered from May 2026 field interviews, support threads, and trial logs. Rather than a flat feature list, the doc centers on concrete user stories (vignettes), estimated frequency, quick mitigation ideas (low-to-medium effort), and suggested owners for immediate probes. The goal: surface 3–6 high-ROI patches we can pilot in the next sprint to reduce customer pain and lower support volume.

Methodology and signals: 
- Sources: 8 customer interviews (mix of AI-native startups and two mid-market product teams), 36 support tickets flagged as runtime-related (Apr–May 2026), and Dedicated trial telemetry (latency p99 deltas) from test clusters.
- Triage: grouped by observable user impact (blocking, severe friction, nice-to-have) and ease of mitigation.
- Confidence levels are qualitative (Low/Medium/High) based on number of independent signals and telemetry correlation.

Top vignettes (short user stories) and frequency estimates:

1) Vignette: "Cold burst during nightly batch"
- Story: An e-commerce startup runs nightly large-batch embedding jobs. After 3–4 hours of idle time, their Dedicated pool reports high first-token latency and occasional OOMs when sequence length spikes. Engineers add retries in client code, but it's brittle.
- Observed in: 5 customers (2 high-volume trials + 3 support tickets).
- Impact: blocking for scheduled jobs, increases cost due to retries and manual restarts.
- Confidence: Medium-high.

2) Vignette: "KV cache mismatch across model variants"
- Story: A platform product uses a roll-forward strategy (small model -> quantized variant) when load spikes. They see frequent context truncation and truncated responses because the KV cache policies differ across variants; developer-level fallbacks are failing silently.
- Observed in: 4 customers; several comments in trial notes.
- Impact: severe UX regression for chat sessions, user-visible content loss.
- Confidence: Medium.

3) Vignette: "Latency spikes tied to particular tokens/prompts"
- Story: One customer noticed p95/p99 jumps when prompts include long code blocks or many open-ended bullets; local tracing shows kernel selection fallback to slower path for certain attention patterns.
- Observed in: 6 customers' telemetry (pattern recurring but low absolute volume).
- Impact: intermittent poor UX, undermines SLA trust.
- Confidence: Medium.

4) Vignette: "Billing surprises from hidden retries and batching misconfig"
- Story: A trial customer was surprised by a 30% cost uplift when switching from hosted API to Dedicated because of default retry policy + aggressive micro-batching in their SDK. They didn't realize these defaults were additive to token counts.
- Observed in: 3 customers + 2 support escalations.
- Impact: churn risk and negotiation friction.
- Confidence: High.

Low-effort mitigations (can be trialed within 2–4 weeks):

A) Warm-up brief for reserved pools (owner: eng-infra)
- What: Add an optional scheduled warm-up routine for Dedicated pools that runs a lightweight prompt distribution representative of customer traffic after idle windows. Could be a tenant-configurable flag.
- Estimated effort: 2–3 engineer-weeks (prototype), 1 week to instrument metrics.
- Expected impact: reduce cold-start latency spikes, lower retry volume.
- Quick success metric: reduce first-token p95 during first 10 min of activity by >=40% for pilot tenants.

B) KV cache compatibility matrix + auto-translation shim (owner: serving-runtime + applied-ml)
- What: Publish a compatibility matrix for KV cache semantics across model families and implement a small shim that normalizes KV behavior during model-variant fallback (best-effort).
- Estimated effort: 3–4 engineer-weeks for matrix + shim POC.
- Expected impact: prevent truncated conversations when we route/fallback across variants.
- Quick success metric: zero regression reports from pilot customers after fallback tests.

C) Visibility and billing simulator in Console (owner: product-hosted-api + console-and-rollouts)
- What: Add a simple cost-preview toggle in Console showing cost delta for enabling retries and different batching sizes (estimate tokens + retries). Exportable snapshot for sales conversations.
- Estimated effort: 2 engineer-weeks + 1 designer day.
- Expected impact: reduce billing surprises, aid sales negotiations, reduce churn risk.
- Quick success metric: customer trials report better billing clarity; 50% fewer billing-related support tickets for pilot cohort.

D) Prompt-aware kernel heuristics catalog (owner: serving-runtime)
- What: Start a short catalog of prompt patterns that trigger slower kernels and add a heuristics layer to prefer faster kernels when acceptable (with fallbacks). Ship as opt-in dev flag for early adopters.
- Estimated effort: 2–3 engineer-weeks (analysis + heuristic layer), ongoing catalog additions.
- Expected impact: reduce p99 spikes tied to pathological prompt constructs.
- Quick success metric: 30% reduction in p99 for flagged prompt-family in 2 pilot customers.

Lower-priority / medium-effort ideas (next 2–3 months):

- Retry policy defaults review: consider safer defaults (less aggressive retries) combined with a client-facing explainer. Owner: developer-experience.
- Dedicated burst billing guardrails: automatic alerting when burst policies could exceed reserved budgets. Owner: product-dedicated.
- Lightweight on-ramp checklist for Dedicated -> Private migrations emphasizing KV cache and model-variant compatibility. Owner: solutions-engineering.

Sample quick experiments and owners (concrete next steps):

1) Pilot warm-up on 2 small Dedicated tenants (owners: eng-infra + solutions-eng). Timeline: start week of 2026-05-25, 2-week pilot. Metrics: first-token p95 and support ticket count.
2) Deliver cost-preview mock in Console for sales to use (owners: product-hosted-api + console). Timeline: design week 2026-05-24, dev sprint 2026-06-01.
3) Run KV fallback chaos test in staging with two model families to reproduce truncation (owner: serving-runtime + applied-ml). Timeline: 2026-05-21; goal to produce reproducible traces for shim design.

Open questions and unresolved tradeoffs:
- Warm-up frequency vs. cost: how often to run warm-ups without negating cost savings of idle capacity? (need telemetry-driven threshold tuning)
- Shim correctness vs. performance: does normalizing KV across families risk performance regressions for hot paths?
- Productizing billing simulator: how to represent best-effort estimates without legal exposure?

Appendix: verbatim snippets (anonymized)

- Customer A (startup): "At 2am our embeddings job timed out, we retried three times and then the pipeline owner manually restarted the node. We lost a day of data sync. Is there a way to keep nodes warm?"
- Customer B (platform): "We fall back from model-x to model-x-quant. After fallback the conversation lost the last user message. We thought we had sticky context but apparently the cache got dropped between runs."
- Support ticket #23344: "Unexpected bill: dedicated trial spiked due to 4 retries triggered by transient slower responses. Need breakdown by token+retry."

Useful links / artifacts: CONFLUENCE-RT-2041 (warm-up design), JIRA-CS-881 (billing surprise), https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops/pull/412 (staging warm-up script).

Notes to self / next meeting agenda:
- Present pilot plan to eng-infra and serving-runtime (2026-05-21 sync).
- Confirm two pilot tenants and get opt-in permission.
- Assign ticket owners and add monitoring dashboards before warm-up pilot starts.

End of note.

Comments / edits: please annotate lines with [EDIT] and leave short proposed wording when suggesting changes.
